summary: Santa Fe County, NM summit in the Pecos Wilderness; a 1916 Forest Service lookout home and shelter were planned there, and the FFLA list marks the site gone.

facts.design: 1916 plan: log cabin with stone and masonry base and steep roof, plus a separate shelter (newspaper report quoted by Forest Lookouts)
facts.status_note: Forest Fire Lookout Association list marks it gone; no removal date or description of remains found

access.note: The trailhead at the Santa Fe Ski Area parking lot is for the peak (SummitPost); no source describes access to the lookout site

visit.trail_note: SummitPost describes a summit route from the Santa Fe Ski Area parking lot trailhead

events.note: Forest Service started work on a new lookout home and a shelter at Lake Peak; the report says no lookout had yet been assigned

evidence.supports: Lake Peak is a summit in the Pecos Wilderness of the Santa Fe National Forest
evidence.quote: Lake Peak is a craggy summit located in the Pecos Wilderness of the Santa Fe National Forest
Lake Peak is located about 20 miles from Santa Fe

evidence.supports: trailhead at the Santa Fe Ski Area parking lot
evidence.quote: The trail head for Lake Peak (and Santa Fe Baldy) is located at the parking lot of the Santa Fe Ski area

evidence.supports: listed as a rock shelter, gone, in Santa Fe County
evidence.quote: Lake Peak Santa Fe 35.79499 -105.76429 Rock Shelter Gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLA list calls the site a rock shelter, while the 1916 newspaper report describes a log cabin on a stone and masonry base with a separate shelter farther up. The report describes a plan, not a finished structure, so the list may describe only the shelter. Not confirmed by any later source.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: the only history is a 1916 newspaper report (The Santa Fe New Mexican, not read directly) quoted on Forest Lookouts, plus the FFLA list line. The FFLA rock-shelter type conflicts with the 1916 log-cabin plan; resolved_conflicts records it. No removal date, staffing after 1916, or site description found. Two searches for a Lake Peak lookout history found nothing; Glorieta Baldy is a different tower. An auto-generated LLMpedia entry was ignored. Brief elevation not verified; the SummitPost text read did not give a figure. Story runs about 220 words.
